## 1. The Inward Umbrella — raw-001

Disposition: REVISION_REQUIRED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 32; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-001

**title:** The Inward Umbrella

**protagonistSuggestion:** Opa

**everydayGoal:** Stay dry in the rain

**primaryObject:** Umbrella

**normalExpectation:** Pressing the button opens the canopy above, creating a dry shield.

**impossibleRule:** The umbrella opens downward, wrapping around the user's body instead of above it, and always migrates to cover the lowest point.

**visibleTrigger:** Opa presses the open button under rain; the canopy blooms down over his arm and torso, leaving his head wet.

**whyThisObject:** An umbrella's entire purpose is to open into a dome over your head; inverting that dome makes it wrap you in wet fabric while rain still hits your exposed head.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The action meant to create dry overhead space instead traps the body and concentrates rain onto the uncovered head, directly preventing dryness.

**frameZeroDescription:** Opa stands in rain with a closed umbrella raised; the button has been pressed but the canopy has opened downward around his arm and upper body, his head exposed to downpour.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Opa pulls the inverted canopy off his head and points the handle skyward, pressing button again to close. visibleConsequence: The wet fabric slides up his arm and seals around his neck like a collar, while rain soaks his exposed face. newInformation: The umbrella can't be removed by pulling; it migrates to the highest point of his body.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Opa crouches low to the ground, hoping the umbrella will slide up to his raised hand. visibleConsequence: The canopy promptly engulfs his crouched back and legs, leaving only his feet sticking out, while rain pools on the fabric. newInformation: The umbrella always moves to cover the lowest body part, not the highest.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Opa lies flat on the ground, spreading arms and legs to prevent any body part from being lowest. visibleConsequence: The umbrella flattens over his entire body like a tarp, but water runs off the edges and forms a puddle around him, soaking him from below. newInformation: Being covered doesn't stop water; it collects and soaks from ground contact.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Opa rolls sideways toward a bus shelter, hoping to escape the rain while still covered. visibleConsequence: The umbrella rolls with him, wrapping around his torso like a soggy cocoon, and his head remains in the rain as he bumps into the shelter wall. newInformation: The umbrella's coverage deflects all rain away from any part it touches, concentrating rain onto uncovered head.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Opa sits up inside the shelter, folds the umbrella manually by hand, and uses it as a normal hat. visibleConsequence: The umbrella stays open upside-down over his head, collecting rainwater that pours down his face inside the shelter. newInformation: The impossible orientation persists even when manually adjusted; any use creates a personal rain cloud.

**finalPayoff:** The umbrella stays open upside-down over his head, collecting rainwater that pours down his face inside the shelter.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** inversion persists despite manual correction

**loopPotential:** Each new body position causes the umbrella to relocate to the lowest point, so Opa keeps trying to out-think the wrap but only changes which part gets covered.

**environment:** Rainy city sidewalk

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** The protective function is reversed into a wet trap; visually clear because a downward-opening umbrella is instantly wrong for staying dry.

        "protagonistGoal": "Stay dry in the rain",
        "objectOrPrimaryInteraction": "Umbrella",
        "impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction": "The umbrella opens downward, wrapping around the user's body instead of above it, and always migrates to cover the lowest point.",
        "frameZeroDescription": "Opa stands in rain with a closed umbrella raised; the button has been pressed but the canopy has opened downward around his arm and upper body, his head exposed to downpour. Opa Opa pulls the inverted canopy off his head and points the handle skyward, pressing button again to close.. The wet fabric slides up his arm and seals around his neck like a collar, while rain soaks his exposed face. The umbrella can't be removed by pulling; it migrates to the highest point of his body.",
        "escalationPlan": [
          {
            "startSeconds": 0.0,
            "endSeconds": 3.0,
            "description": "Opa stands in rain with a closed umbrella raised; the button has been pressed but the canopy has opened downward around his arm and upper body, his head exposed to downpour. Opa Opa pulls the inverted canopy off his head and points the handle skyward, pressing button again to close.. The wet fabric slides up his arm and seals around his neck like a collar, while rain soaks his exposed face. The umbrella can't be removed by pulling; it migrates to the highest point of his body."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 3.0,
            "endSeconds": 6.0,
            "description": "Opa Opa crouches low to the ground, hoping the umbrella will slide up to his raised hand.. The canopy promptly engulfs his crouched back and legs, leaving only his feet sticking out, while rain pools on the fabric. The umbrella always moves to cover the lowest body part, not the highest."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 6.0,
            "endSeconds": 9.0,
            "description": "Opa Opa lies flat on the ground, spreading arms and legs to prevent any body part from being lowest.. The umbrella flattens over his entire body like a tarp, but water runs off the edges and forms a puddle around him, soaking him from below. Being covered doesn't stop water; it collects and soaks from ground contact."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 9.0,
            "endSeconds": 12.0,
            "description": "Opa Opa rolls sideways toward a bus shelter, hoping to escape the rain while still covered.. The umbrella rolls with him, wrapping around his torso like a soggy cocoon, and his head remains in the rain as he bumps into the shelter wall. The umbrella's coverage deflects all rain away from any part it touches, concentrating rain onto uncovered head."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 12.0,
            "endSeconds": 15.0,
            "description": "Opa Opa sits up inside the shelter, folds the umbrella manually by hand, and uses it as a normal hat.. The impossible orientation persists even when manually adjusted; any use creates a personal rain cloud."
          }
        ],

## 2. Self-Squeezing Toothpaste — raw-002

Disposition: REJECTED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 18; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-002

**title:** Self-Squeezing Toothpaste

**protagonistSuggestion:** Kiko

**everydayGoal:** Brush teeth

**primaryObject:** Toothpaste tube

**normalExpectation:** Squeezing tube dispenses paste onto brush.

**impossibleRule:** The tube squeezes itself from the bottom when cap is off, but any paste exiting immediately crawls back inside the nozzle when you squeeze manually.

**visibleTrigger:** Kiko removes cap and paste oozes out on its own; when Kiko squeezes, the paste retracts.

**whyThisObject:** Toothpaste is meant to be pushed out by external pressure; reversing cause and effect makes the tube act like a living creature controlling its contents.

**goalRuleRelationship:** Every attempt to get paste onto brush results in either uncontrollable overflow or instant reattachment to tube, so brushing never gets paste.

**frameZeroDescription:** Kiko holds a toothbrush ready while a toothpaste tube on the counter is already oozing a snake of paste upward; Kiko's other hand reaches to squeeze, but the paste begins sliding back into the nozzle.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Kiko grabs the tube and squeezes hard to force paste onto brush. visibleConsequence: The ribbon of paste outside retracts fully into the nozzle, leaving brush dry. newInformation: Manual squeezing causes paste to be sucked back, opposite of normal.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Kiko holds the tube upright and waits for it to ooze on its own, then brings brush underneath. visibleConsequence: Paste drips onto the brush but continues flowing, wrapping around bristles and gluing them into a blob. newInformation: The tube's self-squeeze never stops, creating an endless stream.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Kiko yanks the brush away to break the paste stream. visibleConsequence: The paste string stretches and snaps, flinging the blob back onto Kiko's nose; the tube continues to ooze a new strand. newInformation: Breaking the stream causes projectile paste, and the tube refills itself instantly.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Kiko caps the tube and uses a finger to scrape paste from his nose onto the brush. visibleConsequence: The tube starts shaking and expands, popping the cap off and spraying paste across the mirror. newInformation: The tube cannot be stopped by capping; pressure builds and releases violently.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Kiko hides the tube in a drawer and quickly rubs the brush with the paste already on it. visibleConsequence: The drawer rattles, the tube rockets out, and a fresh paste snake lands directly on Kiko's tongue. newInformation: The tube actively targets Kiko's mouth, ensuring the paste reaches the goal but not via the brush.

**finalPayoff:** The drawer rattles, the tube rockets out, and a fresh paste snake lands directly on Kiko's tongue.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** absurd success via object's own action

**loopPotential:** Kiko might try closing the drawer, using a different tube, or catching the paste, but the tube always ejects paste onto his tongue exactly when he gives up.

**environment:** Bathroom sink and mirror

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Toothpaste self-dispensing and refilling is a direct function inversion; the tube controls the paste rather than the user.

      "beats": [
        {
          "startSeconds": 0.0,
          "endSeconds": 3.0,
          "description": "Kiko holds a toothbrush ready while a toothpaste tube on the counter is already oozing a snake of paste upward; Kiko's other hand reaches to squeeze, but the paste begins sliding back into the nozzle. Kiko Kiko grabs the tube and squeezes hard to force paste onto brush.. The ribbon of paste outside retracts fully into the nozzle, leaving brush dry. Manual squeezing causes paste to be sucked back, opposite of normal."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 3.0,
          "endSeconds": 6.0,
          "description": "Kiko Kiko holds the tube upright and waits for it to ooze on its own, then brings brush underneath.. Paste drips onto the brush but continues flowing, wrapping around bristles and gluing them into a blob. The tube's self-squeeze never stops, creating an endless stream."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 6.0,
          "endSeconds": 9.0,
          "description": "Kiko Kiko yanks the brush away to break the paste stream.. The paste string stretches and snaps, flinging the blob back onto Kiko's nose; the tube continues to ooze a new strand. Breaking the stream causes projectile paste, and the tube refills itself instantly."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 9.0,
          "endSeconds": 12.0,
          "description": "Kiko Kiko caps the tube and uses a finger to scrape paste from his nose onto the brush.. The tube starts shaking and expands, popping the cap off and spraying paste across the mirror. The tube cannot be stopped by capping; pressure builds and releases violently."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 12.0,
          "endSeconds": 15.0,
          "description": "Kiko Kiko hides the tube in a drawer and quickly rubs the brush with the paste already on it.. The drawer rattles, the tube rockets out, and a fresh paste snake lands directly on Kiko's tongue. The tube actively targets Kiko's mouth, ensuring the paste reaches the goal but not via the brush."
        }
      ],

## 3. Spiraling Shopping Cart — raw-003

Disposition: REJECTED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 19; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-003

**title:** Spiraling Shopping Cart

**protagonistSuggestion:** Mimi

**everydayGoal:** Push cart through supermarket to checkout

**primaryObject:** Shopping cart

**normalExpectation:** All four wheels swivel and roll straight when pushed.

**impossibleRule:** Each wheel locks in alternating directions every time the cart moves, causing cart to travel in tightening spirals toward the store entrance.

**visibleTrigger:** Mimi pushes forward, cart veers left and circles back.

**whyThisObject:** Cart wheels are meant to provide straight mobility; locking their directions converts steering into a chaotic orbit.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The push intended to move cart forward instead causes a spiral away from checkout, preventing reaching the goal.

**frameZeroDescription:** Mimi stands behind a shopping cart in an aisle, hands on handle, but all four wheels are pointed in different fixed angles; the cart has already begun a curved path back toward the entrance doors.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Mimi pushes harder and straightens handle to go down aisle. visibleConsequence: The cart jerks right, then left, tracing a spiral that wraps around a cereal display. newInformation: Force increases turning radius instability, not direction control.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Mimi tries to pull the cart backward, hoping the wheels unlock. visibleConsequence: The cart spins in place like a top, cans rattling, then accelerates forward in a new spiral toward the produce section. newInformation: Backward motion resets wheel angles to new random locks, worsening path.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Mimi leans over and tries to rotate one wheel by hand while holding cart steady. visibleConsequence: The other three wheels snap to new positions, causing the cart to lurch sideways and knock over a stack of oranges. newInformation: Wheel directions are interdependent; adjusting one changes all.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Mimi abandons pushing and drags the cart along the floor by its front corner. visibleConsequence: The cart tilts and rolls on two wheels, then slams down and spirals toward the automatic entrance, triggering doors to open. newInformation: The cart is stable only when moving sideways, but that still leads to exit.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Mimi lets go of the cart and runs toward checkout, hoping to grab items and leave. visibleConsequence: The cart, still spiraling, bumps into Mimi from behind, pushing her through the checkout line and out the exit. newInformation: The cart's uncontrollable motion actively pursues Mimi, forcing her out of the store without paying.

**finalPayoff:** The cart, still spiraling, bumps into Mimi from behind, pushing her through the checkout line and out the exit.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** goal reached wrongly / environmental consequence

**loopPotential:** Any attempt to steer or adjust wheels only creates a new spiral, and the cart inevitably herds Mimi toward the exit.

**environment:** Supermarket aisle with checkout and automatic doors

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Wheels are for straight motion; reversing that into locked spirals is instantly intuitive and blocks shopping goal.

            "startSeconds": 6.0,

## 4. Sweep-Back Broom — raw-004

Disposition: REVISION_REQUIRED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 38; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-004

**title:** Sweep-Back Broom

**protagonistSuggestion:** Arda

**everydayGoal:** Sweep dirt into a dustpan

**primaryObject:** Broom

**normalExpectation:** Sweeping moves dirt forward into a pile.

**impossibleRule:** Dirt swept forward reappears in its original location exactly two seconds later, while the broom's bristles leave a clean trail that slowly fills back.

**visibleTrigger:** Arda sweeps a pile to the dustpan, turns to get pan, and the dirt is already back where it started.

**whyThisObject:** Broom bristles are meant to displace particles; if the displacement is temporary, sweeping becomes a time-delayed loop.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The action of sweeping creates only a brief illusion of cleanliness; dirt returns before it can be collected, preventing the goal.

**frameZeroDescription:** Arda stands with broom in mid-sweep, a neat pile near dustpan; behind him, the original dirt patch is slowly reappearing on the floor.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Arda sweeps quickly and immediately tilts dustpan to catch pile. visibleConsequence: As he tilts pan, the pile dissolves and dirt races back to the original spot, leaving pan empty. newInformation: The delay is exactly two seconds, and any pause lets dirt escape.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Arda sweeps while holding dustpan in the other hand, moving both together. visibleConsequence: Dirt enters the pan but then flies out backward through the bristles, returning to start. newInformation: The broom's bristles repel dirt when the pan is close, so dirt cannot be trapped.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Arda turns the broom over and uses the handle to push dirt like a rake. visibleConsequence: The dirt stays put for a full three seconds, then jumps back even faster, scattering across a wider area. newInformation: Using a non-bristle part changes the delay to three seconds but increases speed of return.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Arda sweeps dirt into an open shoebox and quickly closes the lid. visibleConsequence: The box shakes, dirt bursts out the seams, and returns to the original spot, leaving box empty. newInformation: Containment fails; dirt always phases back to start regardless of barrier.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Arda gives up and simply walks away, leaving the broom on the floor. visibleConsequence: The broom starts sweeping itself in small arcs, and the dirt forms one neat pile in the center of the room. newInformation: The broom can only sweep effectively when no one is trying to collect the dirt.

**finalPayoff:** The broom starts sweeping itself in small arcs, and the dirt forms one neat pile in the center of the room.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** role reversal / object does task when abandoned

**loopPotential:** Arda may return to collect, but then dirt scatters; the broom only succeeds when unattended.

**environment:** Kitchen floor

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Broom's cleaning function is delayed and reversed; the object works only by itself, creating a clear causal joke.

## 5. Vacuum Blows — raw-005

Disposition: REVISION_REQUIRED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 33; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-005

**title:** Vacuum Blows

**protagonistSuggestion:** Luca

**everydayGoal:** Clean crumbs from carpet

**primaryObject:** Vacuum cleaner

**normalExpectation:** Vacuum sucks air and debris into bag.

**impossibleRule:** The vacuum blows air outward instead of sucking, scattering dust and crumbs toward the user's face and across the room.

**visibleTrigger:** Luca turns it on, crumbs fly up and coat his glasses.

**whyThisObject:** Vacuum's core function is negative pressure; reversing polarity turns cleaning into a debris storm.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The action meant to remove crumbs instead propels them everywhere, making the room dirtier and preventing cleaning.

**frameZeroDescription:** Luca pushes a vacuum over a carpet, but a cloud of dust and crumbs is erupting from the nozzle, covering his shoes and floating upward.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Luca checks the bag and points nozzle away, turning it on again. visibleConsequence: A blast of air shoots out, knocking over a plant and spraying soil across the floor. newInformation: The motor polarity is reversed, so it's now a leaf blower.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Luca reverses the vacuum's hose, attaching the other end to the front. visibleConsequence: The machine still blows, but now it sends air into its own bag, inflating it like a balloon until it pops. newInformation: Reversing the hose doesn't change airflow; it just pressurizes the containment.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Luca holds the vacuum bag shut with his hand and tilts the nozzle toward a window. visibleConsequence: The bag inflates, lifts the vacuum off the floor, and starts flying around the room, spraying dust in circles. newInformation: The trapped air turns the vacuum into a thruster, causing uncontrolled flight.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Luca unplugs the vacuum to stop the chaos. visibleConsequence: The vacuum falls to the floor and lets out a final puff of dust that settles exactly back onto the carpet. newInformation: Without power, the debris returns to its original position due to the reversed air pressure.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Luca plugs it back in, but this time turns the power dial to 'max' hoping it will suck. visibleConsequence: The vacuum rockets forward, dragging Luca across the carpet and out the door, leaving a trail of sucked-up crumbs behind. newInformation: Max power reverses thrust direction, so the vacuum now sucks only when moving backward, dragging the user.

**finalPayoff:** The vacuum rockets forward, dragging Luca across the carpet and out the door, leaving a trail of sucked-up crumbs behind.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** cause/result inversion via motion

**loopPotential:** Each correction flips the airflow direction, but always in the opposite of what Luca expects, so he is alternately blown or dragged.

**environment:** Living room

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Vacuum's suction reversed is instantly wrong; causing it to become a thruster adds absurd consequence.

      "beats": [
        {
          "startSeconds": 0.0,
          "endSeconds": 3.0,
          "description": "Luca pushes a vacuum over a carpet, but a cloud of dust and crumbs is erupting from the nozzle, covering his shoes and floating upward. Luca Luca checks the bag and points nozzle away, turning it on again.. A blast of air shoots out, knocking over a plant and spraying soil across the floor. The motor polarity is reversed, so it's now a leaf blower."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 3.0,
          "endSeconds": 6.0,
          "description": "Luca Luca reverses the vacuum's hose, attaching the other end to the front.. The machine still blows, but now it sends air into its own bag, inflating it like a balloon until it pops. Reversing the hose doesn't change airflow; it just pressurizes the containment."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 6.0,
          "endSeconds": 9.0,
          "description": "Luca Luca holds the vacuum bag shut with his hand and tilts the nozzle toward a window.. The bag inflates, lifts the vacuum off the floor, and starts flying around the room, spraying dust in circles. The trapped air turns the vacuum into a thruster, causing uncontrolled flight."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 9.0,
          "endSeconds": 12.0,
          "description": "Luca Luca unplugs the vacuum to stop the chaos.. The vacuum falls to the floor and lets out a final puff of dust that settles exactly back onto the carpet. Without power, the debris returns to its original position due to the reversed air pressure."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 12.0,
          "endSeconds": 15.0,
          "description": "Luca Luca plugs it back in, but this time turns the power dial to 'max' hoping it will suck.. The vacuum rockets forward, dragging Luca across the carpet and out the door, leaving a trail of sucked-up crumbs behind. Max power reverses thrust direction, so the vacuum now sucks only when moving backward, dragging the user."
        }
      ],

## 6. Mirrored Doorway — raw-006

Disposition: REVISION_REQUIRED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 33; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-006

**title:** Mirrored Doorway

**protagonistSuggestion:** Noah

**everydayGoal:** Enter the kitchen from hallway

**primaryObject:** Door

**normalExpectation:** Opening a door leads to the room on the other side.

**impossibleRule:** Whichever side of the door Noah opens, he steps into the same hallway but mirrored left-right.

**visibleTrigger:** Noah opens kitchen door and sees hallway behind him without turning around.

**whyThisObject:** A door is a threshold; if it teleports you back but mirrored, the transition is impossible to complete.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The act of crossing to the kitchen instead returns him to the hallway, preventing the goal.

**frameZeroDescription:** Noah holds a door open; through the doorway is a reversed hallway identical to the one behind him, while a kitchen is visible in the mirror behind him.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Noah steps through the doorway quickly, expecting to enter kitchen. visibleConsequence: He lands in a mirrored hallway, with door now behind him showing the kitchen as a reflection. newInformation: Passing through flips his orientation and swaps which side is real.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Noah backs through the doorway, hoping to reverse the mirror effect. visibleConsequence: He ends up in the original hallway but now the door is on his left instead of right, and the kitchen is behind him. newInformation: Backing through does not cancel the flip; it just reorients his body.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Noah tries to open the door from the mirrored hallway's other side. visibleConsequence: The door opens to an identical mirrored hallway nested inside, and Noah sees multiple copies of himself standing in doorways. newInformation: Each crossing creates a new mirrored copy of the same hallway, like an infinite recursion.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Noah holds the door open with one hand and reaches through to touch the kitchen counter he can see in the reflection. visibleConsequence: His arm disappears through the doorway and emerges from a door behind him, tapping his own shoulder. newInformation: Space is folded so any object poked through wraps around to the starting side.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Noah closes the door entirely, then opens it again while looking at his feet. visibleConsequence: He steps through and finds himself in the kitchen, but everything is mirrored—cabinets open the wrong way, and the clock runs backward. newInformation: The door finally allows entry, but the entire kitchen's handedness is reversed, so using it remains confusing.

**finalPayoff:** He steps through and finds himself in the kitchen, but everything is mirrored—cabinets open the wrong way, and the clock runs backward.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** spatial rule change / goal reached with side effect

**loopPotential:** Every additional door in the kitchen may also be mirrored, leading Noah to question every threshold.

**environment:** Hallway and kitchen doorway

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Door as threshold is subverted by self-mirroring; intuitive because you see same hallway where kitchen should be.

## 7. Backward Alarm Clock — raw-007

Disposition: REVISION_REQUIRED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 46; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-007

**title:** Backward Alarm Clock

**protagonistSuggestion:** Opa

**everydayGoal:** Wake up at 7 AM after setting alarm

**primaryObject:** Alarm clock

**normalExpectation:** Alarm rings at set time; hands move forward.

**impossibleRule:** The clock's hands move backward whenever the alarm is set, so time appears to run in reverse; the alarm rings only when the hands return to midnight.

**visibleTrigger:** Opa sets alarm for 7:00, the hour hand starts cranking counterclockwise.

**whyThisObject:** Clock is meant to measure forward time; reversing hands makes scheduled wake-up impossible.

**goalRuleRelationship:** Setting the alarm to a future time causes the clock to move backward away from that time, so the alarm will never ring at 7 AM.

**frameZeroDescription:** Opa sits up in bed, staring at a bedside clock whose hour hand is moving backward past 6, while the alarm hand points to 7.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Opa manually winds the clock forward to 6:59, expecting the alarm soon. visibleConsequence: As soon as he releases, the hands spin backward rapidly to 3:00. newInformation: Manual forward adjustment is undone by the reverse mechanism.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Opa turns the alarm off and just watches the clock to see what time it shows. visibleConsequence: The hands freeze, then twitch backward one minute for every real second that passes. newInformation: Without alarm set, the clock still runs backward but slower.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Opa sets the alarm for a time that already appears behind the current hand position, like 2:00, hoping it will trigger quickly. visibleConsequence: The alarm rings immediately, but the hands jump forward to noon, and the ringing reverses itself into a silent vacuum of sound. newInformation: Triggering the alarm causes time to jump forward to noon and sound to invert.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Opa unplugs the clock and uses his phone to check the actual time. visibleConsequence: The clock's display reappears on his phone screen, showing the same backward time, and the phone's alarm icon turns into an hourglass. newInformation: The clock's impossible rule spreads to other time-keeping devices.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Opa gives up and falls back asleep. visibleConsequence: The clock chimes twelve times in reverse, and Opa wakes up at 7 AM, but the clock reads 7 PM. newInformation: The backward time eventually catches up to the correct wake hour, but day and night are swapped.

**finalPayoff:** The clock chimes twelve times in reverse, and Opa wakes up at 7 AM, but the clock reads 7 PM.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** delayed consequence / goal reached wrongly via causal inversion

**loopPotential:** If Opa trusts the clock, he'll sleep through day; if he ignores it, he wakes on time but distrusts all clocks.

**environment:** Bedroom with bedside clock

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Clock's directional time reversal directly prevents scheduled waking; the impossible rule is visually obvious with backward hands.

        "objectOrPrimaryInteraction": "Alarm clock",
        "impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction": "The clock's hands move backward whenever the alarm is set, so time appears to run in reverse; the alarm rings only when the hands return to midnight.",
        "frameZeroDescription": "Opa sits up in bed, staring at a bedside clock whose hour hand is moving backward past 6, while the alarm hand points to 7.         "escalationPlan": [
          {
            "startSeconds": 0.0,

            "description": "Opa sits up in bed, staring at a bedside clock whose hour hand is moving backward past 6, while the alarm hand points to 7.           },
          {
            "startSeconds": 3.0,
            "endSeconds": 6.0,
            "description": "Opa Opa turns the alarm off and just watches the clock to see what time it shows.. The hands freeze, then twitch backward one minute for every real second that passes. Without alarm set, the clock still runs backward but slower."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 6.0,
            "endSeconds": 9.0,
            "description": "Opa Opa sets the alarm for a time that already appears behind the current hand position, like 2:00, hoping it will trigger quickly.. Triggering the alarm causes time to jump forward to noon and sound to invert."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 9.0,
            "endSeconds": 12.0,
            "description": "Opa Opa unplugs the clock and uses his phone to check the actual time..           },
          {
            "startSeconds": 12.0,
            "endSeconds": 15.0,
            "description": "Opa Opa gives up and falls back asleep.. The clock chimes twelve times in reverse, and Opa wakes up at 7 AM, but the clock reads 7 PM. The backward time eventually catches up to the correct wake hour, but day and night are swapped."
          }
        ],

## 8. Neighbor's TV Remote — raw-008

Disposition: REJECTED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 18; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-008

**title:** Neighbor's TV Remote

**protagonistSuggestion:** Kiko

**everydayGoal:** Change channel to watch favorite show

**primaryObject:** TV remote

**normalExpectation:** Pressing buttons changes your own TV channel.

**impossibleRule:** The remote's signal always targets the neighbor's television through the wall, changing their channel while your TV stays off.

**visibleTrigger:** Kiko presses power; neighbor yells, but Kiko's TV remains black.

**whyThisObject:** Remote is designed to control one specific TV; misdirecting signal to wrong TV makes it useless for your goal.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The intended action of controlling your TV instead controls someone else's, so your show cannot be selected.

**frameZeroDescription:** Kiko points remote at his dark TV, but through the apartment wall, the neighbor's TV screen is visibly flickering channels, and the neighbor's shouting bubble appears.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Kiko moves closer to his TV, pressing power repeatedly. visibleConsequence: The neighbor's TV volume increases to maximum, shaking the wall, while Kiko's screen stays off. newInformation: Distance doesn't matter; the remote's signal is hardwired to the neighbor's set.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Kiko covers the remote's IR emitter with his hand, hoping to block scatter. visibleConsequence: The neighbor's TV turns off and on rapidly, causing a strobe effect through the window. newInformation: Blocking the emitter still sends an encoded signal that only the neighbor's TV understands.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Kiko opens his TV's manual buttons and tries to change channel directly. visibleConsequence: The neighbor's TV switches to a karaoke channel, and the neighbor starts singing loudly, while Kiko's TV ignores the manual buttons. newInformation: Any input intended for Kiko's TV is transferred to the neighbor's TV due to a crossed signal wire.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Kiko unplugs his TV to 'reset' the remote link. visibleConsequence: The neighbor's TV turns off and then on, now showing Kiko's living room via a hidden camera feed. newInformation: The link is now bidirectional; the neighbor's TV displays Kiko's actions.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Kiko goes next door to ask the neighbor to change their channel to Kiko's show. visibleConsequence: The neighbor agrees, but when they press their own remote, Kiko's TV turns on and changes to a cooking show. newInformation: The cross-wiring is symmetrical: neighbor's remote controls Kiko's TV.

**finalPayoff:** The neighbor agrees, but when they press their own remote, Kiko's TV turns on and changes to a cooking show.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** role reversal / bidirectional transfer

**loopPotential:** Kiko could swap remotes with neighbor, but that might swap their TVs entirely, leading to endless confusion.

**environment:** Apartment living room with thin wall to neighbor

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Remote's targeted control is rerouted to wrong device; visually funny when neighbor reacts and your screen stays dark.

## 9. Ceiling Pancake — raw-009

Disposition: REVISION_REQUIRED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 28; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-009

**title:** Ceiling Pancake

**protagonistSuggestion:** Mimi

**everydayGoal:** Flip a pancake

**primaryObject:** Frying pan

**normalExpectation:** A quick wrist flip sends pancake up and back into pan.

**impossibleRule:** The pan exerts a vertical launch force so strong that any food flies upward and sticks to the ceiling; the pan then becomes too slippery to hold.

**visibleTrigger:** Mimi flips the pancake; it rockets to ceiling and stays.

**whyThisObject:** Pan's function is to toss food for cooking; if toss becomes permanent adhesion, cooking is impossible.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The flipping action meant to turn the pancake instead removes it from the pan and glues it overhead, preventing eating.

**frameZeroDescription:** Mimi holds a frying pan, looking up; a pancake is stuck flat on the ceiling, and a second pancake arcs upward from the pan.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Mimi scrapes the pancake off the ceiling with a spatula, then tries a gentler flip. visibleConsequence: The pancake still leaps up and splats on ceiling, sticking even harder. newInformation: The launch force is independent of wrist strength.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Mimi holds a plate over the pan and flips, hoping to catch the pancake. visibleConsequence: The pancake punches through the plate, sending shards flying, and both pancake and plate fragments stick to ceiling. newInformation: The launched food has enough force to penetrate obstacles.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Mimi turns off the stove and waits for the pancake to fall. visibleConsequence: The pancake slowly peels off the ceiling and falls back into the pan, but immediately turns black and smokes. newInformation: The pancake's fall is controlled by cooking timer, not gravity; it returns overcooked.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Mimi tries to cook without flipping, using a lid to steam. visibleConsequence: The pan's handle starts vibrating, and all the batter in the pan spontaneously flips itself to the ceiling in one big sheet. newInformation: The pan's flipping rule applies to any batter inside, even without a wrist motion.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Mimi gives up and turns off the stove, leaving the pan on the counter. visibleConsequence: The pan itself flips upward, sticks to the ceiling, and the pancake falls onto Mimi's head. newInformation: The pan's upward launch now applies to itself, completing the role reversal.

**finalPayoff:** The pan itself flips upward, sticks to the ceiling, and the pancake falls onto Mimi's head.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** role reversal / object takes action

**loopPotential:** Any cooking utensil in this kitchen may also launch upward, forcing Mimi to cook with ceiling-mounted tools.

**environment:** Kitchen with stove

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Pan's flip function is exaggerated into ceiling adhesion; visually clear and blocks eating.

        "title": "Ceiling Pancake",
        "protagonist": "Mimi",
        "protagonistGoal": "Flip a pancake",
        "objectOrPrimaryInteraction": "Frying pan",
        "impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction": "The pan exerts a vertical launch force so strong that any food flies upward and sticks to the ceiling; the pan then becomes too slippery to hold.",
        "frameZeroDescription": "Mimi holds a frying pan, looking up; a pancake is stuck flat on the ceiling, and a second pancake arcs upward from the pan. Mimi Mimi scrapes the pancake off the ceiling with a spatula, then tries a gentler flip.. The pancake still leaps up and splats on ceiling, sticking even harder. The launch force is independent of wrist strength.",
        "escalationPlan": [
          {
            "startSeconds": 0.0,
            "endSeconds": 3.0,
            "description": "Mimi holds a frying pan, looking up; a pancake is stuck flat on the ceiling, and a second pancake arcs upward from the pan. Mimi Mimi scrapes the pancake off the ceiling with a spatula, then tries a gentler flip.. The pancake still leaps up and splats on ceiling, sticking even harder. The launch force is independent of wrist strength."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 3.0,
            "endSeconds": 6.0,
            "description": "Mimi Mimi holds a plate over the pan and flips, hoping to catch the pancake.. The pancake punches through the plate, sending shards flying, and both pancake and plate fragments stick to ceiling. The launched food has enough force to penetrate obstacles."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 6.0,
            "endSeconds": 9.0,
            "description": "Mimi Mimi turns off the stove and waits for the pancake to fall.. The pancake slowly peels off the ceiling and falls back into the pan, but immediately turns black and smokes. The pancake's fall is controlled by cooking timer, not gravity; it returns overcooked."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 9.0,
            "endSeconds": 12.0,
            "description": "Mimi Mimi tries to cook without flipping, using a lid to steam.. The pan's handle starts vibrating, and all the batter in the pan spontaneously flips itself to the ceiling in one big sheet. The pan's flipping rule applies to any batter inside, even without a wrist motion."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 12.0,
            "endSeconds": 15.0,
            "description": "Mimi Mimi gives up and turns off the stove, leaving the pan on the counter.. The pan itself flips upward, sticks to the ceiling, and the pancake falls onto Mimi's head. The pan's upward launch now applies to itself, completing the role reversal."
          }
        ],

## 10. Kettle Rain Cloud — raw-010

Disposition: REJECTED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 24; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-010

**title:** Kettle Rain Cloud

**protagonistSuggestion:** Arda

**everydayGoal:** Make a cup of tea

**primaryObject:** Kettle

**normalExpectation:** Kettle boils water, steam escapes, hot water pours into cup.

**impossibleRule:** Boiling water evaporates into a small rain cloud that follows the kettle, and the rain falls only when you try to pour, often into your face or elsewhere.

**visibleTrigger:** Arda boils kettle, a mini cloud forms above it; when he tilts, rain falls on his hand.

**whyThisObject:** Kettle's steam should dissipate; if it condenses into a mobile cloud, it steals the water before it can be poured.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The water never stays liquid to pour; it becomes a cloud that rains unpredictably, preventing tea.

**frameZeroDescription:** Arda holds a boiling kettle with a tiny gray cloud hovering just above the spout; small raindrops fall onto his sleeve.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Arda waves away the cloud and quickly pours into a cup. visibleConsequence: The cloud darts under the stream, catching all the water as it pours, leaving the cup dry. newInformation: The cloud can intercept the stream, so water becomes rain before reaching cup.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Arda holds the cup over the kettle spout to catch water before cloud intercepts. visibleConsequence: The cloud squeezes through the spout and rains inside the cup, but the water immediately evaporates back up to the cloud. newInformation: Any liquid water in the cup is reabsorbed by the cloud due to its attachment to the kettle's heat.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Arda puts the kettle in the refrigerator to cool the cloud down. visibleConsequence: The cloud starts snowing, covering Arda's hand and the counter with frost, while the kettle remains hot. newInformation: Cooling the environment changes the cloud's precipitation but not its stealing behavior.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Arda tilts the kettle and holds an umbrella over his head. visibleConsequence: The cloud expands into a full room-wide rainstorm, soaking everything except the cup. newInformation: The cloud's size scales with attempts to shield from it.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Arda unplugs the kettle and uses a microwave to heat water directly. visibleConsequence: The cloud follows the kettle, which now flies off the counter and hovers over the microwave, raining into it and shorting the appliance. newInformation: The cloud is bonded to the kettle object, not the heating method, and it actively prevents any other water heating.

**finalPayoff:** The cloud follows the kettle, which now flies off the counter and hovers over the microwave, raining into it and shorting the appliance.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** environmental takeover / self-created obstacle

**loopPotential:** Arda might use a different kettle, but the cloud may transfer to that one, chasing any boiling attempt.

**environment:** Kitchen counter

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Kettle's steam condensing into a thieving rain cloud is intuitive and directly blocks tea.

      "impossibleRule": "Boiling water evaporates into a small rain cloud that follows the kettle, and the rain falls only when you try to pour, often into your face or elsewhere.",

      "frameZeroDescription": "Arda holds a boiling kettle with a tiny gray cloud hovering just above the spout; small raindrops fall onto his sleeve.       "finalPayoff": "Arda Arda unplugs the kettle and uses a microwave to heat water directly..       "beats": [
        {
          "startSeconds": 0.0,
          "endSeconds": 3.0,
          "description": "Arda holds a boiling kettle with a tiny gray cloud hovering just above the spout; small raindrops fall onto his sleeve. Arda Arda waves away the cloud and quickly pours into a cup.. The cloud darts under the stream, catching all the water as it pours, leaving the cup dry. The cloud can intercept the stream, so water becomes rain before reaching cup."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 3.0,
          "endSeconds": 6.0,
          "description": "Arda Arda holds the cup over the kettle spout to catch water before cloud intercepts.. The cloud squeezes through the spout and rains inside the cup, but the water immediately evaporates back up to the cloud. Any liquid water in the cup is reabsorbed by the cloud due to its attachment to the kettle's heat."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 6.0,
          "endSeconds": 9.0,
          "description": "Arda Arda puts the kettle in the refrigerator to cool the cloud down.. The cloud starts snowing, covering Arda's hand and the counter with frost, while the kettle remains hot. Cooling the environment changes the cloud's precipitation but not its stealing behavior."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 9.0,
          "endSeconds": 12.0,
          "description": "Arda Arda tilts the kettle and holds an umbrella over his head.. The cloud expands into a full room-wide rainstorm, soaking everything except the cup. The cloud's size scales with attempts to shield from it."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 12.0,
          "endSeconds": 15.0,
          "description": "Arda Arda unplugs the kettle and uses a microwave to heat water directly.. The cloud follows the kettle, which now flies off the counter and hovers over the microwave, raining into it and shorting the appliance. The cloud is bonded to the kettle object, not the heating method, and it actively prevents any other water heating."
        }

        "objectOrPrimaryInteraction": "Kettle",
        "impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction": "Boiling water evaporates into a small rain cloud that follows the kettle, and the rain falls only when you try to pour, often into your face or elsewhere.",
        "frameZeroDescription": "Arda holds a boiling kettle with a tiny gray cloud hovering just above the spout; small raindrops fall onto his sleeve. Arda Arda waves away the cloud and quickly pours into a cup.. The cloud darts under the stream, catching all the water as it pours, leaving the cup dry. The cloud can intercept the stream, so water becomes rain before reaching cup.",
        "escalationPlan": [
          {
            "startSeconds": 0.0,
            "endSeconds": 3.0,
            "description": "Arda holds a boiling kettle with a tiny gray cloud hovering just above the spout; small raindrops fall onto his sleeve. Arda Arda waves away the cloud and quickly pours into a cup.. The cloud darts under the stream, catching all the water as it pours, leaving the cup dry. The cloud can intercept the stream, so water becomes rain before reaching cup."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 3.0,
            "endSeconds": 6.0,
            "description": "Arda Arda holds the cup over the kettle spout to catch water before cloud intercepts.. The cloud squeezes through the spout and rains inside the cup, but the water immediately evaporates back up to the cloud. Any liquid water in the cup is reabsorbed by the cloud due to its attachment to the kettle's heat."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 6.0,
            "endSeconds": 9.0,
            "description": "Arda Arda puts the kettle in the refrigerator to cool the cloud down.. The cloud starts snowing, covering Arda's hand and the counter with frost, while the kettle remains hot. Cooling the environment changes the cloud's precipitation but not its stealing behavior."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 9.0,
            "endSeconds": 12.0,
            "description": "Arda Arda tilts the kettle and holds an umbrella over his head.. The cloud expands into a full room-wide rainstorm, soaking everything except the cup. The cloud's size scales with attempts to shield from it."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 12.0,
            "endSeconds": 15.0,
            "description": "Arda Arda unplugs the kettle and uses a microwave to heat water directly..           }

## 11. Dirtying Soap — raw-011

Disposition: REVISION_REQUIRED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 36; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-011

**title:** Dirtying Soap

**protagonistSuggestion:** Luca

**everydayGoal:** Wash hands clean

**primaryObject:** Soap bar

**normalExpectation:** Rubbing soap with water removes dirt.

**impossibleRule:** Soap transfers dirt from the sink onto hands, making them grimier with every scrub; when rinsed, the soap laughs and re-dirties the water.

**visibleTrigger:** Luca rubs soap, hands turn black.

**whyThisObject:** Soap's chemical action is to lift dirt; reversing it makes soap a dirt magnet that deposits grime.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The act of washing applies more dirt, so hands never become clean.

**frameZeroDescription:** Luca stands at sink with soapy hands, but his hands are covered in dark grime, and the soap bar is pristine white while black suds flow down the drain.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Luca rinses hands thoroughly under water. visibleConsequence: The water runs black, but his hands remain black, and the soap bar floats over and touches his elbow, transferring more grime. newInformation: Rinsing does not remove soap's dirt; the soap actively reattaches to skin.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Luca uses a nail brush to scrub the grime off. visibleConsequence: The brush strokes push the grime deeper into his skin, making his hands look like charcoal. newInformation: Any friction with the grime helps it penetrate, not remove.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Luca switches to liquid soap from a bottle. visibleConsequence: The liquid soap pours out as black goo and coats the bar soap, which then leaps into Luca's pocket, staining his clothes. newInformation: All soaps in the environment are contaminated and transfer grime to any surface.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Luca dries his hands with a paper towel. visibleConsequence: The towel tears away a layer of grime but reveals a second layer of different colored dirt underneath. newInformation: The dirt is layered, and removing the top layer just exposes the next.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Luca gives up and leaves the bathroom, hands black. visibleConsequence: The soap bar follows him, bouncing along the floor, and wherever it touches, grime appears, making a trail. newInformation: The soap's dirt-creating ability extends beyond hands to the environment.

**finalPayoff:** The soap bar follows him, bouncing along the floor, and wherever it touches, grime appears, making a trail.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** delayed consequence / environmental spread

**loopPotential:** Luca can try other cleaning products, but they may all become dirt generators due to the soap's influence.

**environment:** Bathroom sink

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Soap's cleaning action reversed into dirt application is a direct function inversion with messy visual payoff.

Luca Luca rinses hands thoroughly under water.. The water runs black, but his hands remain black, and the soap bar floats over and touches his elbow, transferring more grime. Rinsing does not remove soap's dirt; the soap actively reattaches to skin."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 3.0,
            "endSeconds": 6.0,
            "description": "Luca Luca uses a nail brush to scrub the grime off.. The brush strokes push the grime deeper into his skin, making his hands look like charcoal. Any friction with the grime helps it penetrate, not remove."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 6.0,
            "endSeconds": 9.0,
            "description": "Luca Luca switches to liquid soap from a bottle.. The liquid soap pours out as black goo and coats the bar soap, which then leaps into Luca's pocket, staining his clothes. All soaps in the environment are contaminated and transfer grime to any surface."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 9.0,
            "endSeconds": 12.0,
            "description": "Luca Luca dries his hands with a paper towel.. The towel tears away a layer of grime but reveals a second layer of different colored dirt underneath. The dirt is layered, and removing the top layer just exposes the next."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 12.0,
            "endSeconds": 15.0,
            "description": "Luca Luca gives up and leaves the bathroom, hands black.. The soap bar follows him, bouncing along the floor, and wherever it touches, grime appears, making a trail. The soap's dirt-creating ability extends beyond hands to the environment."
          }
        ],

          "visibleConsequence": "The water runs black, but his hands remain black, and the soap bar floats over and touches his elbow, transferring more grime.",

          "strategy": "Luca uses a nail brush to scrub the grime off.",
          "visibleConsequence": "The brush strokes push the grime deeper into his skin, making his hands look like charcoal.",
          "newInformation": "Any friction with the grime helps it penetrate, not remove."
        },
        {
          "strategy": "Luca switches to liquid soap from a bottle.",

          "visibleConsequence": "The towel tears away a layer of grime but reveals a second layer of different colored dirt underneath.",
          "newInformation": "The dirt is layered, and removing the top layer just exposes the next."
        },

          "strategy": "Luca gives up and leaves the bathroom, hands black.",
          "visibleConsequence": "The soap bar follows him, bouncing along the floor, and wherever it touches, grime appears, making a trail.",

## 12. Wet-Transfer Towel — raw-012

Disposition: REJECTED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 18; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-012

**title:** Wet-Transfer Towel

**protagonistSuggestion:** Noah

**everydayGoal:** Dry off after shower

**primaryObject:** Towel

**normalExpectation:** Towel absorbs water from body.

**impossibleRule:** Towel absorbs water from any wet surface but immediately releases it onto any dry surface it touches next, including Noah.

**visibleTrigger:** Noah wraps towel around waist; water pours out onto the floor.

**whyThisObject:** Towel is meant to hold water; if it discharges instantly, drying becomes a game of wet transfer.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The action of drying with towel transfers water back onto body or surroundings, so Noah never stays dry.

**frameZeroDescription:** Noah stands in bathroom with towel around waist, but water is streaming from the towel onto his legs and pooling on the floor.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Noah squeezes the towel over the bathtub to drain it. visibleConsequence: The towel releases a torrent, then immediately reabsorbs water from the air, swelling up. newInformation: The towel can reabsorb water from humidity, so squeezing doesn't empty it.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Noah hangs the towel on a rack and uses a bathrobe instead. visibleConsequence: The towel, hanging, drips continuously onto the bathrobe, soaking it. newInformation: The towel's discharge is constant and targets the driest nearby fabric.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Noah wraps a dry hand towel around his head. visibleConsequence: The hand towel soaks up water from his hair and then squirts it onto the mirror, fogging it. newInformation: Towels transfer water to mirrors and glass, not just skin.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Noah uses a hairdryer to dry himself without a towel. visibleConsequence: The hanging towel leaps off the rack and wraps around Noah's leg, transferring moisture back onto his skin. newInformation: The towel actively seeks the driest body part to wet.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Noah runs out of the bathroom naked, hoping to air dry. visibleConsequence: The towel follows him, wrapping around his waist, and immediately releases a bucket of water onto the living room carpet. newInformation: The towel is attached to Noah's body and will never let him be dry.

**finalPayoff:** The towel follows him, wrapping around his waist, and immediately releases a bucket of water onto the living room carpet.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** object attachment / goal never reached

**loopPotential:** Any attempt to get dry with a towel simply relocates the wetness, often back to Noah.

**environment:** Bathroom and adjacent living room

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Towel's absorbency reversed into discharge is clearly wrong; the chase adds physical comedy.

          "description": "Noah stands in bathroom with towel around waist, but water is streaming from the towel onto his legs and pooling on the floor.         {

          "endSeconds": 6.0,

        "impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction": "Towel absorbs water from any wet surface but immediately releases it onto any dry surface it touches next, including Noah.",
        "frameZeroDescription": "Noah stands in bathroom with towel around waist, but water is streaming from the towel onto his legs and pooling on the floor.         "escalationPlan": [

            "description": "Noah stands in bathroom with towel around waist, but water is streaming from the towel onto his legs and pooling on the floor.           },
          {
            "startSeconds": 3.0,
            "endSeconds": 6.0,
            "description": "Noah Noah hangs the towel on a rack and uses a bathrobe instead.. The towel, hanging, drips continuously onto the bathrobe, soaking it. The towel's discharge is constant and targets the driest nearby fabric."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 6.0,
            "endSeconds": 9.0,
            "description": "Noah Noah wraps a dry hand towel around his head.. The hand towel soaks up water from his hair and then squirts it onto the mirror, fogging it. Towels transfer water to mirrors and glass, not just skin."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 9.0,
            "endSeconds": 12.0,
            "description": "Noah Noah uses a hairdryer to dry himself without a towel.. The hanging towel leaps off the rack and wraps around Noah's leg, transferring moisture back onto his skin. The towel actively seeks the driest body part to wet."
          },

          }

## 13. Tangling Hairbrush — raw-013

Disposition: REVISION_REQUIRED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 31; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-013

**title:** Tangling Hairbrush

**protagonistSuggestion:** Opa

**everydayGoal:** Brush hair smooth

**primaryObject:** Hairbrush

**normalExpectation:** Brushing untangles hair and smooths it.

**impossibleRule:** Each brush stroke creates a new knot, and the knots tighten the more you brush; hair eventually coils around the brush like a topiary.

**visibleTrigger:** Opa brushes once, hair stands up in a giant knot.

**whyThisObject:** Brush bristles are meant to separate strands; if they weave strands together, brushing becomes tangling.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The action of brushing makes hair worse, so smooth hair is impossible.

**frameZeroDescription:** Opa stands in front of mirror holding a brush, but his hair is a twisted bird's nest with the brush embedded in it.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Opa pulls the brush out slowly, hoping to unwind the knot. visibleConsequence: The knot tightens into a bun that pulls his head back. newInformation: Pulling the brush out causes the hair to cinch, not loosen.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Opa uses a wide-tooth comb to gently work through the tangle. visibleConsequence: The comb adds more knots, and his hair expands into a giant sphere around his head. newInformation: Any grooming tool multiplies knots instead of removing them.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Opa applies hair conditioner to make strands slippery. visibleConsequence: The hair becomes like rubber, and the brush bounces off, but the knots stretch and snap back with more loops. newInformation: Conditioner turns hair elastic, making tangles spring-loaded.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Opa puts on a hat to hide the hair and stop brushing. visibleConsequence: The hat is sucked into the hair-knot and swallowed, disappearing into the tangled mass. newInformation: The hair's tangling now acts like a living trap, consuming objects.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Opa uses scissors to cut the hair away. visibleConsequence: The hair regrows instantly into a larger, tighter knot, trapping the scissors. newInformation: Cutting triggers accelerated regrowth with more tangles.

**finalPayoff:** The hair regrows instantly into a larger, tighter knot, trapping the scissors.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** logical extreme / effort worsens

**loopPotential:** Opa can try different tools, but the hair always re-tangles and often captures the tool.

**environment:** Bathroom with mirror

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Brush's detangling function reversed into knot-creation is visually clear; regrowth adds escalation.

## 14. Self-Healing Paper — raw-014

Disposition: MALFORMED; eligibility: None; SFE: None; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-014

**title:** Self-Healing Paper

**protagonistSuggestion:** Kiko

**everydayGoal:** Cut paper for craft

**primaryObject:** Scissors

**normalExpectation:** Scissors shear paper into two pieces.

**impossibleRule:** As scissors cut, the paper immediately heals behind the blades, leaving no cut; the scissors themselves become slightly more blunt.

**visibleTrigger:** Kiko snips a paper, the cut line closes seamlessly.

**whyThisObject:** Scissors are meant to divide material; if the material self-heals, the cutting action is futile.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The intended cut never persists, so crafting cannot proceed.

**frameZeroDescription:** Kiko holds scissors mid-snip on a paper; the cut line behind the blades is sealing itself closed, with no separation visible.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Kiko cuts faster, moving scissors along a straight line. visibleConsequence: The paper zips back together instantly, and the scissors make a zipper-like sound. newInformation: Speed of cutting increases the healing speed equally.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Kiko folds the paper and cuts through multiple layers. visibleConsequence: The layers fuse together at the cut line, creating a thicker uncut stack. newInformation: Cutting multiple layers causes them to weld, not separate.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Kiko uses a craft knife instead of scissors. visibleConsequence: The knife blade passes through but the paper instantly reattaches, and the knife's edge dulls to a butter knife shape. newInformation: The self-healing effect applies to any cutting tool and dulls the blade.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Kiko tries to tear the paper by hand. visibleConsequence: The paper stretches like rubber and bounces back, flipping out of his hands. newInformation: The paper has become elastic, so it cannot be cut or torn.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Kiko gives up and tries to use pre-cut paper shapes from a packet. visibleConsequence: The pre-cut shapes snap back into full sheets, and the scissors in his hand leap to the paper and start 'cutting' but leaving no marks. newInformation: The rule reverses relationship: tools cuts but material refuses to remain divided; even pre-existing cuts are undone.

**finalPayoff:** The pre-cut shapes snap back into full sheets, and the scissors in his hand leap to the paper and start 'cutting' but leaving no marks.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** false assumption / effort negated

**loopPotential:** Any future cutting attempt heals; Kiko might try water or fire, but risk of new escalation.

**environment:** Craft table

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Scissors' dividing function is negated by self-healing paper; intuitive because cut line zips shut.

## 15. Bottom-Opening Zipper — raw-015

Disposition: REJECTED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 18; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-015

**title:** Bottom-Opening Zipper

**protagonistSuggestion:** Mimi

**everydayGoal:** Zip up jacket to stay warm

**primaryObject:** Jacket zipper

**normalExpectation:** Pulling zipper up closes the jacket.

**impossibleRule:** As you pull the zipper tab upward, the bottom of the zipper separates, so the jacket opens from bottom while top closes; when you pull down, the bottom closes but top opens.

**visibleTrigger:** Mimi zips up to neck; the jacket's bottom half splits open, exposing her stomach.

**whyThisObject:** Zipper is designed to interlock teeth sequentially; if it opens opposite end, the closure is incomplete.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The action to close the jacket creates an opening elsewhere, so warmth cannot be retained.

**frameZeroDescription:** Mimi holds zipper tab at neck, jacket top is closed, but the bottom half hangs open, cold air whooshing through.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Mimi pulls zipper down to close the bottom gap. visibleConsequence: The bottom zips shut but the top splits down to her chest. newInformation: The zipper has a pivot point; one end opens as the other closes.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Mimi holds the bottom together with one hand while zipping up with the other. visibleConsequence: The zipper teeth at her hand pop apart, and her fingers get caught between them. newInformation: Physical holding doesn't prevent separation; the zipper actively parts around any obstruction.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Mimi zips halfway, hoping the middle stays closed. visibleConsequence: Both top and bottom open outward like a mouth, and the jacket flaps open completely. newInformation: Halfway position opens both ends simultaneously.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Mimi turns the jacket inside out and zips from the other side. visibleConsequence: The zipper now unzips from the middle, splitting the jacket into two separate halves that fall to the floor. newInformation: The zipper's failure mode changes with orientation, now bisects the garment.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Mimi grabs a safety pin to pin the bottom closed. visibleConsequence: The safety pin zips itself into the zipper track and the entire jacket rolls up like a window blind, squeezing Mimi's torso. newInformation: The zipper treats any inserted object as a pull tab and activates full closure upward, trapping Mimi.

**finalPayoff:** The safety pin zips itself into the zipper track and the entire jacket rolls up like a window blind, squeezing Mimi's torso.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** unexpected causal chain / self-trapping

**loopPotential:** Further attempts to unfasten may cause the jacket to roll or unroll unpredictably.

**environment:** Cold windy street

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Zipper's interlocking action is spatially inverted, so closing one end opens the other; visually clear and blocks warmth.

          "description": "Mimi Mimi holds the bottom together with one hand while zipping up with the other.. The zipper teeth at her hand pop apart, and her fingers get caught between them. Physical holding doesn't prevent separation; the zipper actively parts around any obstruction."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 6.0,
          "endSeconds": 9.0,
          "description": "Mimi Mimi zips halfway, hoping the middle stays closed.. Both top and bottom open outward like a mouth, and the jacket flaps open completely. Halfway position opens both ends simultaneously."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 9.0,
          "endSeconds": 12.0,
          "description": "Mimi Mimi turns the jacket inside out and zips from the other side.. The zipper now unzips from the middle, splitting the jacket into two separate halves that fall to the floor. The zipper's failure mode changes with orientation, now bisects the garment."
        },
        {
          "startSeconds": 12.0,
          "endSeconds": 15.0,
          "description": "Mimi Mimi grabs a safety pin to pin the bottom closed.. The safety pin zips itself into the zipper track and the entire jacket rolls up like a window blind, squeezing Mimi's torso. The zipper treats any inserted object as a pull tab and activates full closure upward, trapping Mimi."
        }
      ],

        "impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction": "As you pull the zipper tab upward, the bottom of the zipper separates, so the jacket opens from bottom while top closes; when you pull down, the bottom closes but top opens.",
        "frameZeroDescription": "Mimi holds zipper tab at neck, jacket top is closed, but the bottom half hangs open, cold air whooshing through. Mimi Mimi pulls zipper down to close the bottom gap..         "escalationPlan": [
          {
            "startSeconds": 0.0,
            "endSeconds": 3.0,
            "description": "Mimi holds zipper tab at neck, jacket top is closed, but the bottom half hangs open, cold air whooshing through. Mimi Mimi pulls zipper down to close the bottom gap.. The bottom zips shut but the top splits down to her chest. The zipper has a pivot point; one end opens as the other closes."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 3.0,
            "endSeconds": 6.0,
            "description": "Mimi Mimi holds the bottom together with one hand while zipping up with the other.. The zipper teeth at her hand pop apart, and her fingers get caught between them. Physical holding doesn't prevent separation; the zipper actively parts around any obstruction."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 6.0,
            "endSeconds": 9.0,
            "description": "Mimi Mimi zips halfway, hoping the middle stays closed.. Both top and bottom open outward like a mouth, and the jacket flaps open completely. Halfway position opens both ends simultaneously."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 9.0,
            "endSeconds": 12.0,
            "description": "Mimi Mimi turns the jacket inside out and zips from the other side.. The zipper now unzips from the middle, splitting the jacket into two separate halves that fall to the floor. The zipper's failure mode changes with orientation, now bisects the garment."
          },
          {
            "startSeconds": 12.0,
            "endSeconds": 15.0,
            "description": "Mimi Mimi grabs a safety pin to pin the bottom closed.. The zipper treats any inserted object as a pull tab and activates full closure upward, trapping Mimi."
          }
        ],

## 16. Bottomless Backpack — raw-016

Disposition: REVISION_REQUIRED; eligibility: INELIGIBLE; SFE: 36; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-016

**title:** Bottomless Backpack

**protagonistSuggestion:** Arda

**everydayGoal:** Pack backpack for school

**primaryObject:** Backpack

**normalExpectation:** Items placed in top stay inside until you open it.

**impossibleRule:** The bottom of the backpack opens whenever it is upright; when turned upside down, the bottom seals but the top opens, so contents always spill.

**visibleTrigger:** Arda puts books in upright backpack; they fall through bottom onto floor.

**whyThisObject:** Backpack is a container; if gravity works against the orientation, it cannot hold items.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The act of placing items inside directly causes them to exit through bottom, preventing packing.

**frameZeroDescription:** Arda holds a backpack upright with several books halfway falling through the open bottom, while the top zipper is closed.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Arda turns the backpack upside down to use the sealed bottom as top. visibleConsequence: The original top zipper opens, and books pour out onto his head. newInformation: The pack has two openings, and gravity always finds the open one.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Arda holds the backpack sideways and loads books through the side. visibleConsequence: A new side seam splits open, and all contents slide out horizontally. newInformation: Any orientation creates a new opening at the lowest point.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Arda stuffs clothes into the bottom to block it, then adds books. visibleConsequence: The clothes squeeze through the bottom seam, pulling the books with them, leaving an empty flattened pack. newInformation: The bottom opening acts like a drain that vacuums contents out.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Arda puts the backpack on his back, hoping body pressure seals the bottom. visibleConsequence: The pack inflates and launches off his shoulders, spinning in midair as contents rainbow out. newInformation: Wearing the pack triggers ejection, not sealing.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Arda gives up and carries books in his arms. visibleConsequence: The backpack slides over and swallows the books from his arms, then spits them out the bottom into a neat pile at his feet. newInformation: The pack wants to be filled but immediately empties itself as soon as it contains anything.

**finalPayoff:** The backpack slides over and swallows the books from his arms, then spits them out the bottom into a neat pile at his feet.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** impossible containment / object agency

**loopPotential:** Any future loading attempt triggers the same drain; Arda might need a bottomless bag that is actually bottomless.

**environment:** Bedroom floor

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Backpack's containment is inverted by gravity-dependent openings; the drain-like bottom is visually clear.

## 17. Self-Tucking Bed Sheets — raw-017

Disposition: MALFORMED; eligibility: None; SFE: None; ranking: None

### A. Provider raw idea

**ideaId:** raw-017

**title:** Self-Tucking Bed Sheets

**protagonistSuggestion:** Luca

**everydayGoal:** Get out of bed in the morning

**primaryObject:** Bed sheet

**normalExpectation:** You push sheets off and stand up.

**impossibleRule:** The more you push sheets away, the tighter they tuck around your body; sheets re-tuck themselves under the mattress as you move.

**visibleTrigger:** Luca throws off blanket; it snaps back over him.

**whyThisObject:** Bedsheets are meant to cover; if they actively trap, getting up becomes a wrestling match.

**goalRuleRelationship:** The action to remove sheets causes them to rewrap, preventing standing.

**frameZeroDescription:** Luca lies in bed with one leg out, but the sheet has wrapped around his leg and is pulling him back toward the mattress.

**Beat 1:** strategy: Luca sits up and pushes the sheet to the foot of the bed. visibleConsequence: The sheet springs back and tucks itself under his chin, pinning his arms to his sides. newInformation: The sheet's fabric is elastic and self-tucking.

**Beat 2:** strategy: Luca rolls toward the edge to slide out. visibleConsequence: The sheet rolls with him, winding around his torso like a burrito. newInformation: Moving doesn't loosen; it increases winding.

**Beat 3:** strategy: Luca kicks violently to break the wrap. visibleConsequence: The sheet stretches into ropes that tie his ankles to the bed frame. newInformation: The sheet can transform into adjustable restraints, comedic but not harmful.

**Beat 4:** strategy: Luca tries to crawl out from the bottom of the bed. visibleConsequence: The fitted sheet pops off the mattress and becomes a parachute, dragging him back to the center. newInformation: The whole sheet detaches and acts as a net.

**Beat 5:** strategy: Luca calls for help, and Mimi enters to pull him out. visibleConsequence: The sheet wraps around both of them, tucking them together like a mummy, while the bed bounces. newInformation: The sheet's tucking extends to anyone who tries to intervene.

**finalPayoff:** The sheet wraps around both of them, tucking them together like a mummy, while the bed bounces.

**suggestedPayoffFamily:** goal blocked by self-tucking / role reversal

**loopPotential:** Any morning, Luca will be held by sheets until the bed decides to release him.

**environment:** Bedroom

**dialogueNeed:** NONE

**durationSeconds:** 15

**providerRationale:** Bedsheets' covering function becomes trapping; intuitive because throwing off sheets should free you, not rewrap you.
